rubric.why: Mucus protects the stomach wall from its acidic contents.
rubric.description: States that mucus lines the inner wall and protects it from acid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the mucus lining and its protective role against acid.

rubric.why: The epithelial tissue secretes gastric juice and its components support digestion.
rubric.description: States that gastric juice contains pepsinogen for protein digestion and hydrochloric acid to activate pepsinogen to pepsin.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying gastric juice secretion and its roles in protein digestion and pepsinogen activation.

modelAnswer: The mucus lines the inner wall and protects it from acid. This tissue also secretes gastric juice that contains enzyme pepsinogen for protein digestion and hydrochloric acid for activating pepsinogen to pepsin enzyme.

rubric.why: The smooth muscles’ contraction and relaxation drive stomach movement.
rubric.description: States that the smooth muscles contract and relax.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both contraction and relaxation.

rubric.why: Mixing brings food into contact with gastric juice.
rubric.description: States that the muscle action mixes food with gastric juice.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the muscles mix food with gastric juice.

modelAnswer: These muscle contract and relax to mix food with the gastric juice.

rubric.why: This describes the structure of the palisade mesophyll cells.
rubric.description: States that the cells are tightly packed and elongated.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the tightly packed arrangement and elongated shape.

rubric.why: The palisade mesophyll is the leaf tissue where photosynthesis occurs.
rubric.description: Identifies the mesophyll as the site of photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that photosynthesis occurs in the mesophyll.

modelAnswer: It consists of tightly packed elongated cells. Mesophyll tissue is the site of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: This captures the definition of homeostasis, including stability despite external change.
rubric.description: Defines homeostasis as maintaining a stable internal environment despite changes outside the body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the ability to maintain a stable internal environment despite changes in the external environment.

rubric.why: Normal extracellular conditions are necessary for cells to function properly.
rubric.description: Explains that proper cell functioning depends on extracellular conditions being kept in the normal range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking normal extracellular conditions to proper cell functioning; relevant conditions may include temperature, pH, salts, glucose, or oxygen.

modelAnswer: Homeostasis is defined as the ability of an organism to maintain a stable internal environment of the body despite changes in the external environment. The proper functioning of cell is possible only when extracellular conditions such as temperature, pH, and the concentrations of salts, glucose and oxygen are kept in normal range.
